Dose-response model selection

Source: R/mselect.R
mselect.Rd

Re-fits a dose-response model with alternative dose-response functions and compares the resulting fits. The original model is always included.

Usage

mselect(
  object,
  fctList = NULL,
  nested = FALSE,
  sorted = c("IC", "Res var", "Lack of fit", "no"),
  linreg = FALSE,
  icfct = AIC
)

Arguments

object

A fitted object of class "drc".

fctList

An optional list of dose-response functions to fit to the same data. The original model is included even when it is not repeated in this list.

nested

Logical; if TRUE, report p-values from tests comparing each model with the model immediately above it in the returned table. These tests are meaningful only when each pair is nested and is otherwise comparable. The first row has no comparison and its p-value is NA.

sorted

Criterion used to order the result. "IC" (the default) orders by the information criterion in ascending order; "Res var" orders by residual variance in ascending order; "Lack of fit" orders by lack-of-fit p-value in descending order; and "no" preserves the input order. Missing values are placed last.

linreg

Logical; if TRUE, also fit linear, quadratic, and cubic polynomial regressions. This option is available only for continuous data with a single dose-response curve.

icfct

Function used to calculate the information criterion. Defaults to AIC; BIC can also be used. The function must return one numeric value for a fitted model.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per model (including the original model) and columns for the log likelihood, information criterion, lack-of-fit p-value, and, for continuous data, residual variance. If nested = TRUE, a nested-test p-value column is also included unless linreg = TRUE.

Details

The returned matrix reports the log likelihood, the selected information criterion, the lack-of-fit p-value, and (for continuous data) the residual variance. Smaller information-criterion and residual-variance values indicate a better fit; a larger lack-of-fit p-value indicates less evidence of lack of fit. A lack-of-fit p-value is NA when the fit type does not provide this test. Log likelihoods should only be compared for models fit to the same data under comparable likelihoods.

Candidate models are re-fitted to the data stored in object. A candidate that cannot be fitted is retained in the result with NA statistics and a warning. mselect() returns a comparison table, not the fitted candidate objects. With the default sorted = "IC", the first row is the model with the smallest information criterion.

For nested comparisons, each p-value compares a row with the row immediately above it after sorting. Thus, the selected sorted criterion determines the comparison sequence. Failed fits have NA statistics; a nested comparison is omitted if either model in that pair failed. A test error or invalid p-value is reported as NA with a warning. These tests should not be used to compare non-nested models.

Author

Christian Ritz

Examples

## Fit a starting model to the ryegrass data
ryegrass.m1 <- drm(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, fct = LL.4())

## Compare candidate dose-response functions; the smallest AIC is ranked first
candidate_fcts <- list(LL.3 = LL.3(), W1.4 = W1.4(), W2.4 = W2.4())
selection <- mselect(ryegrass.m1, fctList = candidate_fcts)
selection
#>         logLik       IC Lack of fit   Res var
#> W2.4 -15.91352 41.82703   0.9450714 0.2646283
#> LL.4 -16.15514 42.31029   0.8664830 0.2700107
#> W1.4 -17.46720 44.93439   0.4505676 0.3012075
#> LL.3 -18.60413 45.20827   0.3531679 0.3153724

## Identify and refit the AIC-selected model
best_name <- rownames(selection)[1]
best_fit <- if (best_name == ryegrass.m1$fct$name) {
  ryegrass.m1
} else {
  update(ryegrass.m1, fct = candidate_fcts[[best_name]])
}
best_name
#> [1] "W2.4"
best_fit$fct$name
#> [1] "W2.4"

## Add polynomial regressions to the comparison
mselect(ryegrass.m1, fctList = candidate_fcts, linreg = TRUE)
#>          logLik        IC Lack of fit   Res var
#> W2.4  -15.91352  41.82703   0.9450714 0.2646283
#> LL.4  -16.15514  42.31029   0.8664830 0.2700107
#> W1.4  -17.46720  44.93439   0.4505676 0.3012075
#> LL.3  -18.60413  45.20827   0.3531679 0.3153724
#> Cubic -25.53428  61.06856          NA 0.5899609
#> Quad  -35.11558  78.23116          NA 1.2485122
#> Lin   -50.47554 106.95109          NA 4.2863247

## Compare adjacent models in the returned order
mselect(ryegrass.m1, fctList = list(LL.5()), nested = TRUE)
#>         logLik       IC Lack of fit   Res var Nested F test
#> LL.4 -16.15514 42.31029   0.8664830 0.2700107            NA
#> LL.5 -15.87828 43.75656   0.8538476 0.2777393     0.5134602
